hook: She followed every rule. The city still *closed her door.*
dek: The wall above Aries Fish Market in the Bronx started leaning. The owner is asking DOB for one thing: let her use the side door.

slides.label: The market
slides.text: *Aries Fish Market* sits at 748 Lydig Ave in *Pelham Parkway*, the Bronx. Owner *Gisele Blanco* went to high school with our founder, Danny.

slides.label: The wall
slides.text: On *Oct. 22*, a DOB inspector saw the parapet *leaning* over two storefronts. The next day, DOB ordered a fence around the front, out to the curb.

slides.label: Not her fault
slides.text: Gisele didn't break a rule. Under city rules, fixing the wall is the *property owner's job*. She says her landlord waited *two weeks* on the engineer's report.

slides.label: The side door
slides.text: Her building has a side door on *Holland Ave*, about *48 feet* from the danger zone. DOB told her to send reports and pictures. *She did.*

slides.label: No-show
slides.text: DOB confirmed a *2 PM* visit that morning. Two o'clock came. Three o'clock came. *Nobody showed up.* Then she was told items were missing.

slides.label: The math
slides.text: Report filed Monday. About *two weeks* of DOB review. Then the repair. "In two months, I'm going to end up *losing everything*."

slides.label: The ask
slides.text: Not the front door. Just the side door, for *pickups, DoorDash and Uber Eats*, while the landlord fixes the wall. Her team needs the work.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: @nyc_dob, @nycmayor: send an inspector to *748 Lydig Ave*. If that side door is safe, *let her open it.* Safety and survival aren't a trade.

yt_title: Bronx Fish Market Closed by a Leaning Wall: Owner Asks DOB for One Door
caption_instagram:
A Bronx fish market owner followed every rule. The city still closed her door. 🐟

Aries Fish Market on Lydig Ave in Pelham Parkway has been behind a construction fence since Oct. 23, after DOB found the wall above it leaning over the storefronts. Nobody argues with that. Safety first.

But owner Gisele Blanco (who went to high school with our founder) didn't break a rule. Fixing the wall is the property owner's job, and she says she has spent two weeks waiting on the landlord's engineer report. In the meantime she asked to serve customers from her side door on Holland Ave, about 48 feet from the danger zone. She sent DOB everything it asked for. She says inspectors confirmed a 2 PM visit, then never came.

Now she's looking at up to two months closed. "In two months, I'm going to end up losing everything."

Her ask is small: the side door, for pickups, DoorDash and Uber Eats, until the wall is fixed.

@nyc_dob @nycmayor, one inspection at 748 Lydig Ave could keep a Bronx business and its whole team working. Please take a look.

caption_linkedin:
A small business owner followed every rule. A wall she doesn't own closed her door.

Aries Fish Market on Lydig Avenue in the Bronx has been fenced off since October 23, after the NYC Department of Buildings found the parapet above it leaning over the storefronts. Safety first, no argument.

But the repair is the property owner's job, and owner Gisele Blanco says she spent two weeks waiting on her landlord's engineer report. She asked DOB to let her serve customers from a side door about 48 feet from the danger zone, sent the reports and pictures DOB asked for, and says inspectors confirmed a visit that never happened.

She is now looking at up to two months closed, with her team out of work.

This is the gap small businesses fall into: the danger is real, the order is fair, and the person who pays for the delay did nothing wrong. A narrow, temporary path, like a safe side entrance for pickups and delivery, keeps people employed while the fix gets done.

NYC Department of Buildings, Office of the Mayor: one inspection could keep this business alive.
